note: The epochs of data/labels.jsonl. Read by src/labels/batches.ts and ml/batches.py so the eval scripts and the UI cannot disagree about which rows may be scored on. First match wins.

batches.name: Triage of the live list
batches.population: Live PENDING candidates that passed the gate
batches.why: The UI hides each row's score, verdict and source, but the batch is the top of the model's own ranking, ordered best-first. Observed base rate 0.778 against 0.221 and 0.140 for the other two epochs - a labeller notices that within a few rows, and the rate decays as he descends the order. Blind per item, not blind as a set.
batches.use: Training only. Every yes is also a job worth applying to, which is the point: scrolling a page of 800 is not a decision procedure.

batches.name: Stored rejects
batches.population: rejected_jobs, which the first batch could not reach because rejects were not stored yet
batches.why: Drawn after the development set was already spent, labelled without any of these being seen, and never used for tuning. The only unbiased measurement in the project.
batches.use: Evaluation. Touched once - see ml/holdout.py. Tuning anything in response spends the one clean number available.

batches.name: Stratified by source and gate outcome
batches.population: The whole corpus, stratified by source crossed with gate pass/reject
batches.why: A real probability sample: sampling_prob and stratum_size are stored, so estimates can be reweighted to the population, and it includes rows the gate rejected, which is what makes recall computable at all.
batches.use: Development set, and contaminated. Roughly a dozen experiments were run against it - feature sets, thresholds, ordinal versus binary, four classifier families - each choice made while looking at these labels. Cross-validation does not undo that. Fine for training and for cross-validated comparison, not for a number you quote.
